page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.8xlarge is a general purpose, network-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The system features 32 dedicated physical cores using AWS Neoverse-V2 processors operating at 2.8 GHz, with a 1:1 mapping of virtual CPUs to physical cores without hyper-threading. The CPU cache layout provides 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance provides a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no local storage, and does not include hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional memory and multi-core throughput alongside high networking capacity. Memory subsystems achieve top-tier performance, with large block read throughput reaching 412.91 GB/sec and large block write speeds reaching 198.33 GB/sec. Geekbench multi-core performance scores in the top 10% at 21,484.0, complemented by strong code compilation throughput of 49,450.0 and strong multi-threaded decompression at 357.08 GB/sec. Data-intensive benchmarks show top-tier execution, with PassMark database operations measuring 47,617.22 and Redis achieving 66.38 million SET operations per second. Static web serving throughput is similarly strong at 71.82 GB/sec.

Single-core compute throughput remains in the average band across stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations, indicating that performance scales primarily via parallel core utilization. The absence of local NVMe storage requires external network-attached EBS volumes for persistent data storage, making the instance dependent on network connectivity for disk I/O. Furthermore, LLM inference benchmarks show limitations, particularly in small-model text generation where token generation ranks in the lower tiers, reflecting the absence of discrete matrix and vector accelerator extensions.

Amazon Web Services m8gn.8xlarge offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive, highly parallelized workloads by leveraging high memory bandwidth and dedicated Graviton cores without hyper-threading contention. The instance is well-suited for high-throughput in-memory data stores, Redis clusters, relational and non-relational database operations, network-bound web serving fleets, and large-scale software build environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.8xlarge is a general purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System with 32 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz and 128.0 GB of system memory. Lacking local storage and discrete GPUs, the instance relies on remote network storage and provides a 100 Gbps network bandwidth baseline. Empirical benchmarks demonstrate top-tier memory bandwidth, reaching 412.91 GB/sec for uncached reads, coupled with top-tier Geekbench multi-core scores of 21,484.0 and strong multi-threaded decompression. Data workloads excel, logging top-tier PassMark database operations and 66.38 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread CPU performance sits within the average tier, the high parallel core count and exceptional memory throughput make this instance cost-effective for multi-threaded compilation, high-concurrency web serving, Redis caching tiers, and enterprise database workloads.
